transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Is this chair okay? Oh, good, thank you. 

Well, I'm here because... well, I hope I don't sound unreasonable. I try very hard to be a good tenant and not be a bother to anyone. But for months now, I've been dealing with a rather stressful situation at my apartment. It seems the property manager and certain people in the building are... well, they're coordinating things to pressure me out of my apartment. 

I know how that might sound, I really do, and I wouldn't bring it up if I wasn't absolutely sure. But it's these little things—using misdelivered mail, making these perfectly timed noises in the walls, and dropping little comments when I pass them in the hall. I've tried to be polite about it, and they always have some sort of paperwork or explanation ready. But my background is in management analysis, so looking at variables is what I do, and no amount of their explanations changes the pattern I can clearly see. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it in a way that doesn't make me sound difficult, because I'm really not trying to be.
Do you think these people are targeting you specifically?

Well... yes. I do. And I—I really hate to say that, because I know how self-important it sounds, doesn't it? Like I think I'm the center of the universe. I promise you, I don't think that at all, doctor. I'm just a quiet man. 

But... yes, it is directed at me. I wouldn't have believed it myself, but the way the property manager and those specific people operate... it's just too focused to be random. Like I was saying, the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls that are timed exactly to when I sit down to read in the evenings, the little comments from the neighbors... it's all tailored to my routine. 

They always have their paperwork and their polite explanations ready when I ask about it, and I always smile and accept them because I really don't want to be a difficult tenant. I hate making a fuss. But... well, I analyze data for a living, and no amount of their paperwork or explanations changes the pattern I can clearly see. It's all designed to pressure me out of the apartment. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being unreasonable or paranoid? I just want to be completely honest with you, and I hope I'm explaining it properly.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misinterpreting these events?

Oh, I... I completely understand why you would ask that. It's a very fair question, doctor, and I don't blame you for asking it at all. Believe me, I really wish I was just... getting it wrong. It would be so much easier if it were just a simple misunderstanding on my part. 

But... well, as I mentioned, it's been going on for months now. The property manager and those certain people in the building... they really are using the misdelivered mail, the timed noises in the walls, the little comments to pressure me out of the apartment. I know I'm repeating myself, and I'm so sorry to be a broken record. It's just... I've looked at it from every angle, and no amount of their paperwork or their polite explanations changes the pattern I can see. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound stubborn or... or uncooperative to say that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the facts exactly as they are. Am I doing okay explaining this?
Do you think anyone else has noticed these things happening to you?

Oh, um... well, no, not that I'm aware of. I haven't really... I haven't brought it up to anyone else, to be perfectly honest. 

I wouldn't want to be a bother to my friends or family with my apartment troubles, you know? I try very hard to just keep things pleasant and focus on them when I do see people. And... well, I suppose the things that are happening are so tailored to my own daily schedule that a guest probably wouldn't even catch on anyway. 

I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm isolating myself or... or being secretive! I promise I'm not. I just prefer to handle my own affairs quietly without making a fuss or dragging anyone else into it. Do you... do you think I should be asking other people if they notice it? I just want to make sure I'm going about this the right way.
Do you think there's anything that could convince you that these events are not actually happening as you perceive them?

Oh... that's a very thoughtful question. I really appreciate you asking that, doctor, because it shows you're being very thorough with me. And I want to be a good patient for you, I really do. I... I truly wish I could say yes. It would be such an enormous relief to find out I'm just making a silly mistake and that everything is fine. 

But... well, I know I'm repeating myself, and I'm so sorry to keep bringing it back to this, but I'm here because for months now, the property manager and those certain people in the building have been using the misdelivered mail, the timed noises in the walls, and the little comments from the neighbors to pressure me out of my apartment. Because of my training as an analyst, I just can't ignore the data right in front of me. No amount of their paperwork or their polite explanations changes the pattern I can see so clearly. 

I really hate to sound inflexible. I promise you, I'm normally a very agreeable person, and I hate to disagree with you. I just can't un-see what's happening. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as difficult or closed-minded. I just want to give you the most honest answer I can. Am I doing okay?
Do you think there's anything that could change your mind about the property manager and the neighbors trying to pressure you out of your apartment?

Oh, I... I know you just asked me something very similar, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record. I know it must be frustrating to hear me say the same things over and over. I promise I'm really trying to be open-minded, doctor, I truly am. 

It's just... well, like I was saying, it's been going on for months. The property manager, those specific people in the building... they're using the mail, the noises in the walls, the little comments... all of it is just so clearly designed to pressure me out of the apartment. I really wish there was something that could change my mind. I'd love to just accept their paperwork and their polite little explanations and go back to normal. But... well, I can see the pattern. It's just right there. 

I'm so sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. I really don't want to be a difficult patient. I just... I can't ignore what's happening. Is it okay that I feel this way? I hope I'm not disappointing you with my answers.
Do you think the property manager and neighbors would stop pressuring you if you were to move to a different apartment within the same building?

Oh, um... moving to another unit in the same building? I... I haven't actually thought about that. That's a very creative suggestion, doctor, it really is. You always have such interesting ways of looking at things. 

I suppose... well, I'm not entirely sure. On the one hand, it might be nice to have a different view, maybe a little more afternoon sun? But... if it's the same property manager handling the paperwork, and the same neighbors in the halls... I just don't know if a different floor number would really change the... the atmosphere, you know? 

But honestly, I haven't put any thought into a transfer like that. Do you... do you think that's something I should be looking into? I'd be happy to ask the leasing office about their transfer policies if you think it would be a good step for me. I just want to make sure I'm doing what's best, and I really value your opinion on this. Does that sound like a reasonable plan to you?
Why do you think the property manager and neighbors want to pressure you out of your apartment?

Oh, goodness. That is... well, that's the million-dollar question, isn't it? You really do know how to get right to the heart of things, doctor. I appreciate how thorough you are. 

To be completely honest with you... and I feel a little, well, a little foolish admitting this, given my background in analysis... I just don't know. I really don't have a clear answer for you. 

I've looked at the situation from every angle, trying to figure out what I could have possibly done to upset them. I always try to be such a courteous neighbor, you know? I keep my head down, I pay my rent early... I'd just be absolutely mortified if I had accidentally offended someone or been a bother. The very thought of it makes me quite embarrassed, actually. I really hate the idea of being a nuisance to anyone, and it hurts to think they dislike me this much.

But as for their specific reasons for wanting me out... I'm really in the dark. I wish I could give you a better explanation, I truly do. I know you're trying to help me figure this out, and I want to give you everything you need. Is it... is it okay that I don't have all the pieces to the puzzle yet? I hope I'm still doing alright with your questions.
Have you ever felt like someone was out to get you or plotting against you before this situation with your apartment?

Oh, um... before this? No, no, I really don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to get along with everyone, you know? At work, in my personal life... I really pride myself on being a team player and a good colleague. 

I know it might sound strange that this is happening now, out of the blue, and I really hope it doesn't make me seem... well, paranoid or anything. I promise I'm usually very level-headed. In my line of work as an analyst, you really have to be objective and look at the facts. So, no, I've never had any issues like this before. I've always had wonderful relationships with my coworkers and neighbors in the past. 

Does that make sense, doctor? I hope it doesn't seem like I'm making this all up just because it's a new situation for me. I really am trying to give you the most accurate history I can. Am I answering your questions the way you need me to?
Have you ever had any other experiences where you felt like you were being targeted or plotted against, aside from this situation with your apartment?

Oh, um... I think, well, like I was just saying a moment ago, I really haven't. I'm sorry, did I not explain that clearly enough before? I'd hate to think I was being confusing. I always want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to do your job. 

But no, truly, aside from this current trouble at the building, I've never felt like anyone was out to get me or plotting anything. Throughout my whole career and my personal life, I've always had such wonderful, cooperative relationships with people. In management analysis, you really have to build consensus, so I'm usually the one helping to smooth over conflicts, not involved in them! 

So this whole situation right now is just... very out of character for my life. I really don't have a history of having conflicts with people or feeling targeted at all. I hope it's okay that my answer is still the same on that. I just want to be as honest and helpful as possible. Are we... are we on the right track here, doctor? Did I misunderstand the question?
Have you felt like you're being targeted by the property manager and neighbors every day since this started, or are there days when you don't feel that way?

Oh, well... to be completely honest, doctor, it really does feel like it's every single day. I know that probably sounds a bit much, and I wish I could say there were days when things were just quiet and normal... I really do. It's actually a little embarrassing to admit how long it's been happening, because I feel like a competent person should have been able to resolve a misunderstanding by now, you know? 

But... well, this has been going on for about 11 months now. It started shortly after I moved into the new apartment. I hope I don't sound too, well, obsessive or difficult by keeping track of it like that. It's just that it began almost right after I unpacked my boxes, and it just hasn't let up since. 

Is that... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope I'm answering this the right way for your notes. I really just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible.
Do you think the property manager and neighbors would be plotting against anyone else in the building if you were to move away?

Oh, um... you know, I really haven't thought about that. I suppose... well, I really don't think so. I don't want to speak poorly of them, but it feels very specifically directed at me. 

I mean, I haven't noticed them treating anyone else in the building this way. Everyone else seems to come and go without any trouble at all. It's just... it's just my mail that gets tampered with, and my schedule they seem to be tracking. I really hope it doesn't sound arrogant or self-centered to say that I think I'm the only one they're focused on. I certainly don't want to give the impression that I think I'm that important! 

But no, I honestly don't know if they would bother anyone else if I left. I just know what I've been experiencing. Does that... does that answer your question, doctor? I hope I'm not sounding too defensive about it. I just want to give you the most accurate picture I can.
How long have you felt like the property manager and neighbors have been plotting against you?

Oh, um, I think... well, I actually just mentioned this a moment ago, but I know we're covering a lot of ground, so I don't mind repeating it at all! I want to make sure you have everything you need. 

It's been about 11 months now. Like I said, it started right after I moved into the building. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm following your process correctly. Did I... did I miss part of the question earlier, or is there something specific about the timeline you need me to clarify? I'm happy to go over it again if it helps!
Did anything significant happen in your life around the time you first started noticing these things with your property manager and neighbors?

Oh, gosh... significant? Well, I mean, moving is always a bit of a transition, isn't it? I retired a few months before I moved, actually. I was a management analyst for... oh, a very long time. So there was that change, I suppose. 

But other than retiring and then finding the new apartment, I don't think there was anything... unusual. I certainly hope I didn't do anything to, you know, draw this kind of attention to myself when I arrived. I've always tried to be a very quiet, respectful neighbor. 

I'm sorry, I'm not sure if that's what you meant by significant. Was there a particular kind of event you were asking about? I want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think your beliefs about the property manager and neighbors will ever change?

Change my mind? Oh, um... I really do want to be open-minded, doctor. I promise I'm trying to be reasonable about all of this. I know how important that is, and I certainly don't want to be a difficult patient or seem stubborn to you. 

It's just... well, for months now, it's been a constant stream of things. The property manager and certain people in the building... they've been using the misdelivered mail, and these... these timed noises in the walls, and just little comments here and there to pressure me out of the apartment. 

They've given me explanations, of course, and shown me paperwork to try and explain it all away. And I want to accept it, I really do! But... no amount of their paperwork or explanations changes the pattern I can clearly see. It's right there in front of me, day after day, and I can't just ignore it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely unreasonable? I'm really trying my best to handle this politely, I just have to be honest with you about what I'm experiencing. Am I... am I making sense, doctor? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think there's any evidence that could prove to you that the property manager and neighbors are not plotting against you?

Evidence... oh, um. Well, I suppose anyone should be willing to look at evidence, shouldn't they? I really do want to be the kind of person who listens to reason. I know it's so important to be cooperative. 

But, well, like I mentioned just a moment ago—and I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm explaining this clearly for your notes—I've been dealing with this for months. The property manager, and those specific neighbors... they've been doing all of it. The mail being put in my box by mistake on purpose, the noises they make in the walls at very specific times, the little comments they drop when I walk by... all to pressure me to leave. 

And they have shown me things, you know? They've brought out their paperwork and given me all sorts of explanations to try and prove they aren't doing it. And I've looked at it! I really have tried to see their side of it, because I want to be fair. But... none of it changes the actual pattern I'm seeing every single day. 

So, I don't know what kind of evidence could prove they aren't doing it, because I'm living through it, you see? I hope that doesn't make me sound stubborn, doctor. I really am trying to be objective about this. Does that... does that answer your question alright? I can try to explain it differently if that wasn't what you were looking for.
Have you ever found any concrete proof, like a recording or a witness, that supports your belief that the property manager and neighbors are plotting against you?

Concrete proof? Oh... um. Like a tape recording or a video? No, I... I haven't done anything like that. 

I really wouldn't want to do something that feels, well, invasive, you know? I've always prided myself on being a respectful gentleman, and sneaking around trying to record people just seems so... impolite. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was being a nuisance or a troublemaker. I hope you don't think less of me for not having something like that to show you.

And as for witnesses... well, I live alone, so it's really just me experiencing it. The timing of the noises in the walls and the little comments in the hall, it always seems to happen when there's no one else around. I haven't tried to drag any of my other neighbors or guests into it because I really don't want to cause a fuss or make anyone uncomfortable. 

I'm just trying to handle it all as quietly and properly as I can. Is... is that alright, doctor? I hope I'm not disappointing you by not having a tape or a photograph to hand over. I just want to make sure I'm going about this the right way.
Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small, for the events you've been experiencing with your property manager and neighbors?

Other explanations? Oh, um... well, I really have tried to think of some. I promise you, doctor, I don't want to jump to conclusions or be... well, unreasonable. I've spent hours trying to convince myself that maybe the mail really is just a simple postal error, or that the noises are just the building settling. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt. 

But... well, as I was saying before—and I'm sorry to keep bringing it back to this, I just don't know how else to make sense of it—the pattern is just too precise. For months now, the property manager and those certain people in the building... they've been using that misdelivered mail, and those perfectly timed noises in the walls, and the little comments as I walk by, all specifically to pressure me out of my apartment. 

I really wish there was another explanation. And like I said, they give me their excuses and show me their paperwork, and I try so hard to accept it because I want to be agreeable. I really do! But no amount of their paperwork or explanations changes the pattern I can clearly see right in front of me. As an analyst, I'm trained to look at data, and it just doesn't fit any other explanation, no matter how hard I try to find one. 

I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound inflexible or difficult? I'm just trying to give you the most honest answer I can. Am I doing alright, doctor? I really want to make sure I'm cooperating the way you need me to.
Do you think your beliefs about the property manager and neighbors could be a misunderstanding or misinterpretation of their actions?

A misunderstanding? Oh, um... well, I suppose that's always a possibility in life, isn't it? I certainly don't want to be the sort of person who assumes the worst of people. I really do try to be understanding and forgiving. I hope you can see that I'm trying my best not to be accusatory.

But... well, I know I keep repeating myself, and I really apologize for that, I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information... it's just that it's been going on for months now. And it's not just one isolated incident, you see? It's the property manager and those specific people in the building. It's the mail they keep putting in my box on purpose, the noises they time perfectly in the walls, the little remarks they make just as I pass by... all of it designed to pressure me out of my apartment. 

I really wish it was just a misunderstanding. That would be so much easier, wouldn't it? But when you look at the whole picture... well, no amount of their paperwork or the explanations they give me changes the pattern I'm seeing. 

I hope you don't think I'm being paranoid or... or difficult by saying that. I just want to be truthful with you about what I'm experiencing. Does that make sense, doctor? I really hope I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
